children: , the integrated oil-and-gas powerhouse, fell 0.9% to $160.78 Fridaybut America's diesel crunch is handing its refineries a monster opportunity. The U.S. diesel crack spread recently smashed a record $108.02 per barrel as average pump prices reached an all-time high of $5.820 per gallon.

Exxon is built for this moment. Energy Products delivered $5.47 billion, or nearly 38%, of its $14.53 billion in second-quarter earnings after the company produced more diesel than in any previous second quarter. Cash kept roaring in, with operating cash flow hitting $23.56 billion and free cash flow reaching $17.2 billion.

Crack spreads are not pure profit because refining, transportation and hedging costs still bite. But margins this extreme could give Exxon's downstream engine enough muscle to cushion weaker crude prices. The catch is valuation: at $160.78, the stock stands 26.75% above its $126.85 GF Value estimate. The diesel boom is powerful, but Wall Street is not getting Exxon cheaply.

title: Exxon Falls While Diesel Margins Explode to $108
